competitors.name: Bond Bakery Brands / Holy Napoli Pizza
competitors.action: Bond Bakery Brands invested in Holy Napoli Pizza, a Neapolitan-style frozen pizza and dough producer already distributed in 400+ Canadian retail stores, giving a premium artisan freezer brand fresh capacity and distribution fuel.

competitors.name: Nestlé / DiGiorno
competitors.action: DiGiorno rolled out a new Wood Fired Style Crust line in four SKUs for nationwide retail distribution starting in May, a clear incumbent push toward more artisan crust cues like char, chew, and pizzeria-style texture.

competitors.name: CAULIPOWER
competitors.action: CAULIPOWER launched new high-protein single-serve personal pizzas with 21g protein and began rolling them into Hy-Vee, FreshDirect, and additional retailers, signaling the freezer aisle is still chasing protein-forward, portion-controlled pizza formats.

trends.topic: Frozen pizza innovation is clustering around sharper format claims, not generic premium language
trends.magnitude: Today's strongest signals were artisan-investment scale-up, wood-fired crust imitation at mass retail, and protein-forward single-serve pizza expansion.
trends.context: Real Dough should keep its sourdough story extremely concrete. The aisle is rewarding products that can be explained fast: true artisan process, distinct crust experience, or a functional nutrition hook.

market_data.change: Bond investment aimed at increasing production capacity and distribution
Available starting in May at MSRP $6.49
Now in Hy-Vee and FreshDirect with further rollout to Earth Fare, Raley's, Tony's, MOMs, AWG, New Seasons, Bashas' and more

breaking.headline: The freezer aisle is getting more specific: artisan-backed scale, wood-fired crust theater, and protein-led convenience are all advancing at once.
breaking.impact: Real Dough should resist vague premium positioning and keep sharpening a one-line shelf claim around authentic sourdough craft and crust quality, because competitors are making their promises simpler and louder.
